newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slips off highs, support intact.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slips off highs, support intact.

text.p: White sugar futures held on to most of the day's earlier gains on Thursday but a static raws market helped keep activity subdued in London despite the recent physical buying, traders said.

Nearby spreads hovered around flat to 80 cents as May and August firmed slightly to come into line with March, which by 1658 GMT stood 80 cents higher at $302.00. Traders said while chart support seemed to be holding at the psychological $300 barrier, the spot position was unlikely to rally much above the session high of $302.70. "They tried to get it up this morning and there was a little resistance around $302.50," said one trader.
Light mixed buying of March dominated most of the session but ranges across the board were all under $2.00.
May was up 30 cents at $301.20 and August up $1.00 at $302.00, bringing May/August into a small contango. Volume amounted to 1,437 lots, mostly in March.
Technical analysts said they remained neutral towards the spot whites position while values steered clear of the 40-day moving average (MA), currently standing at $303.50.
"The market does remain shy of the MA but as the market has not broken the previous low at $295.10, we remain somewhat neutral at present," said Darren Gurner, an analyst at Sucden.
March's 30 and 40-day averages have already converged, while the 10 and 20-day averages are hovering around $305 and above.
Other technical indicators suggest a movement to the upside.

The contract's slow stochastic lines have crossed in oversold territory and are now approaching neutral above the 30-value buffer, while short-term momentum indicators are also sloping higher out of oversold.
Traders said both the whites and raws markets had largely ignored the fresh fundamental news which emerged on Thursday.
Turkey was believed to have sold 50,000 tonnes of whites to two local companies and Syria bought 26,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar for delivery between Feburary 15 and March 17.
Japanese company Tomen was named as the supplier of 13,000 tonnes of whites at $344 per tonne and the other cargo of 13,000 tonnes of raws was bought from French trader Lorico at $290.40.
Results are still awaited in Libya's whites buying tender and a deal has been reached in Colombia to end the port strike at the Pacific port of Buenaventura.
Nearby positions clawed their way higher on the Paris market in a light total volume of 428 lots. March and May were both up $1.00 at $302.00.
